questions.q: How are dashboard widgets generally presented in the Salesforce mobile app?
options: In the same wide grid as desktop
In a single scrolling column, in reading order
As a slideshow that plays automatically
Only as tables
questions.explain: On a phone, widgets are generally stacked in one column following their desktop reading order.

questions.q: Which widget type is generally the most phone-friendly?
options: Scatter chart
Metric
A ten-column table
A multi-series line chart with many categories
questions.explain: A metric shows one large number readable at a glance. Dense charts and wide tables read poorly on a small screen.

questions.q: Do you need to build a separate dashboard for mobile, per this lesson?
options: Yes, always
Yes, but only for tables
No, design one dashboard that works on both by leading with metrics and keeping it simple
Mobile does not support dashboards at all
questions.explain: A few design habits let a single dashboard serve both desktop and phone.

questions.q: What is the best way to test a dashboard for mobile?
options: Resize your desktop browser and assume it's identical
Check the source report's row count
Read the dashboard's description
Open it in the mobile app as a viewer, with the audience's level of access
questions.explain: Testing on a real device as a viewer catches legibility and access problems the builder view hides.

questions.q: Why should you be careful about stating exact mobile behavior as permanent fact?
options: Mobile features vary by Salesforce release and app configuration, so confirm on your own device
Mobile never changes
Mobile behavior is the same in every org, forever
Dashboards cannot be viewed on mobile
questions.explain: The mobile experience changes with releases and admin configuration, so lean on durable design principles and verify specifics.
